source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Chronic venous insufficiency with impaired venous return and venous hypertension.","B":"Peripheral arterial disease presenting primarily as exertional claudication that improves with rest.","C":"Acute deep vein thrombosis as the usual explanation for years of bilateral varicosities and stasis skin changes.","D":"A normal age-related change that needs no vascular assessment when edema improves with elevation."}}
source_row.rationale: Chronic venous insufficiency commonly causes lower-extremity edema, aching/heaviness, varicosities and skin changes. Symptoms often worsen with prolonged standing and improve with rest or elevation.

source_row.stem: A client has chronic lower-leg swelling, aching and heaviness, varicose veins, and skin changes that worsen after prolonged standing and improve with elevation. Which condition best matches this pattern?
